summary: Tie the sanitisation exemption to the parameter that carries a CLI-built date rather than to the value's shape, and send an ISBN in both spellings the archive stores.
reason: The first version of the guard exempted any value made only of digits and separators, and an ISBN-13 written the way ISBNs are written - 978-88-7524-166-7 - is exactly that, so it went through untouched and biblioteca cerca --isbn kept receiving the portal refusal this whole change exists to remove. Measured 2026-09-06: the portal answers (QR999) Operando con crt non validi, a refusal that carries a QRxxx code just like the threshold one, so the malformed-query detection had to stop keying on the absence of a code. The forms are now named one by one (a plain number, the ISIS range 260101/261231, an ISO date or range) and everything else is sanitised. Sanitising an ISBN is not enough on its own, and the right rewrite is not deducible from the value: two numeric fields of the same archive behave oppositely - on --dewey "340.5" the dot separates two real tokens and the spaced form finds the record, while an ISBN's punctuation formats a single number. The archive is also inconsistent with itself: record 9788875241667 is stored as one token and comes back only from the joined form, while another is stored as "978 88 98231-25-6" and comes back only from the spaced form. Neither spelling alone covers the catalogue, so an identifier field sends both in OR. The perimeter had to narrow twice, and for the same reason both times: a value does not say on its own whether it is a date, the field it sits in does. Keying on the characters let an ISBN-13 through; keying on the date shape let a date searched as TEXT through - ddl cerca --testo "2026-07-01", a document quoting that date, which is a legitimate question and left as ... E (2026-07-01) and came back refused. The exemption now names the two parameters whose value the CLI builds (--data, and --anno on the ddl archive, both compiled into 260101/261231), with the shape check kept alongside so a --data written in a form nobody recognises is neither silently rewritten nor sent as if valid.
validated_outcome: biblioteca cerca --isbn "978-88-7524-166-7" goes from a portal refusal to the right record, leaving as ((9788875241667 O (978 88 7524 166 7)).ISBN); --isbn "978-88-98231-25-6", stored with separators, returns its own record from the same expression, and each spelling alone returns zero on the other one. --dewey "340.5" keeps the spaced rewrite that finds its record. A date range reaching BuildQuery unnormalised stays verbatim and is still refused loudly rather than answered wrongly. ddl cerca --testo "2026-07-01" goes from a portal refusal to rows, leaving as (2026 07 01), while --data 2026-07-01:2026-07-31 and --anno 2026 still compile to 260701/260731 and 260101/261231 untouched.
